enquiry: We manufacture tablets from a powder blend containing an active pharmaceutical ingredient and excipients. Laboratory checks tell us whether the blend is on target, but results arrive after the material has moved through the press. We want to assess whether a fiber based measurement in the feed frame could follow API concentration changes. Our first pilot should compare reasonable measurement options before we commit to production equipment.

intake.summary: The customer wants to assess if a fiber-based measurement in the feed frame can track API concentration changes in a powder blend.

assessment.brief_answer: To track API concentration in the tablet press feed frame, start by testing Near-Infrared (NIR) diffuse reflection spectroscopy, which is the established method for powder blend potency monitoring. Alternatively, evaluate Raman spectroscopy to check for fluorescence interference. A pilot laboratory trial using representative powder samples and independent reference assays will determine the optimal single-method or combined optical configuration.

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data from different sources into a new matrix where variables are placed sequentially.
items.how_it_applies: This approach could be evaluated to combine multiple spectral inputs, though its added value should be tested against single-method models.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The reviewed data fusion concepts stem from general literature and might not directly transfer to powder blend measurements in a feed frame.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
